subject: The 'save democracy' chase
alt: Satish Acharya's two-part cartoon. In the top frame an old man with a white beard and glasses, wearing an orange jacket, and behind him a bald man in a brown jacket, both stretch out their arms and shout with mouths wide open; the speech bubble says in English: 'SAVE DEMOCRACY!'. In the lower part the frame is gone and the whole scene shows: the same two are running and shouting 'SAVE DEMOCRACY!'. The man in the orange jacket holds a chain marked 'CENSORSHIP', and the man in the brown jacket holds a spiked stick marked 'POLICE BRUTALITY'. On the left a figure in tricolour clothes is running for its life, a blue sash on its shoulder reading 'DEMOCRACY'. A newspaper lying on the ground reads: 'BJP'S SAVE DEMOCRACY MARCH'. On the right is the cartoonist's signature: SATISH ACHARYA.
chutki: The top frame is what the camera is meant to show: two leaders, outstretched arms, raised voices and a slogan, 'Save democracy!'. Acharya simply removes the frame. The slogan stays the same, but its meaning turns over. Now we see that the two are not saving anyone; they are chasing someone, one holding the chain of censorship, the other the spiked stick of police brutality. The one running ahead has a word on its shoulder: democracy.

The joke lies in the distance between the slogan and the hand. The newspaper on the ground reports a 'Save Democracy March', but the picture asks who is saving and who is running. When sticks fall on people sitting on the road and locks are put on speech, a march held in the name of that same democracy starts to look less like a slogan and more like a chase.
